title: observability: token-level cost/latency metrics, tracing spans, dashboards and alert tuning
author: Evan Brooks
description:
Motivation: customers need finer-grained observability to debug cost/latency regressions introduced by batching, quantization profiles, and KV-cache behavior. This PR adds token-level cost and latency metrics, improved tracing spans for the serving runtime and batching scheduler, prebuilt Grafana dashboards, and tuned alerts to reduce noise while preserving signal.

What changed (high level): updated runtime instrumentation to emit per-token timing and cost attribution, added KV-cache hit/miss metrics and per-model cost tags, added Otel span instrumentation for batch scheduling/dispatch and kernel selection, implemented Prometheus exporters for token-level metrics, created a set of dashboards for token cost/latency breakdowns and tracing drilldowns, and adjusted default alert rules to be SLO-aware (alert if 99th percentile token latency regresses by >25% or unit-cost rises >30% for 10m).

Compatibility and rollout: changes are backwards compatible (most metrics are additive). New high-cardinality tags (model_version, quant_profile) are optional behind a feature flag controlled by telemetry config to limit cardinality for early rollout. Dashboards are published to the Console but can be toggled per-tenant. Alerts are staged in a canary folder and will be soft-alerting (pager suppressed) for two weeks before full activation.

Testing: unit tests for metric emission and span attributes, integration tests that run against a local OpenTelemetry collector and Prometheus instance, e2e observability smoke tests in CI that verify dashboard queries and alert rule expressions. Load-tested the new metrics pipeline with a synthetic 5k rps workload to confirm exporter throughput and storage cardinality with feature flag off.

Follow-ups: adding sampled request IDs in sampled traces to link tokens -> requests in external tracing UIs, and an SDK helper for customers to attach deterministic prompt groups for cheaper aggregation.

Related: ENG-3721 (token metrics schema), ENG-3778 (alert tuning), SUP-221 (customer-reported cost regression investigation).
commits_summary: Initial instrumentation: emit token_duration_ms and token_cost_usd in runtime telemetry
Add KV cache hit/miss counters and tags (model_version, quant_profile behind flag)
Otel spans: batch_scheduler, kernel_selector, kv_cache_lookup with relevant attributes
Prometheus exporter and aggregation helpers for 99/95/50p token latency and per-token cost
Console: Grafana dashboard JSON, alert rules, docs and rollout config
review_comments: Aisha Kapoor: Can we keep the model_version tag behind the telemetry feature flag by default to avoid cardinality spikes? Also request a short runbook describing how to disable the new metrics per-tenant.
Evan Brooks: Good point — model_version and quant_profile are behind feature flag 'telemetry.high_cardinality'. Added a canary rollout plan and runbook in docs. See updated docs in this PR.
Diego Martinez: Tracing spans look fine, but please add duration_ms attribute on kernel_selector spans to make hotspot queries easier. Also suggest adding sampling for high-frequency model types.
Evan Brooks: Added duration_ms and a sampling config for traced models. Default sampling rate is 0.1 for high-throughput models and can be overridden per-tenant.
Priya Nair: Alert thresholds look noisy in staging — can we change the alert to require 2 consecutive evaluation windows (10m) before firing and add a suppression window for deploys?
Evan Brooks: Changed alert rule to 2 windows and added deploy-suppression label guidance in the console alert docs.
release_notes: Added token-level cost and latency metrics, KV-cache hit/miss metrics, improved tracing spans for batch scheduler and kernel selector, new Console dashboards for token cost/latency breakdowns, and tuned alerting rules (soft-alerting canary rollout). Feature flags protect high-cardinality tags.
